comparisons.peer_topic: Redemption Rights and Depositary Share Structures
comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation may redeem most preferred stock series at its option at liquidation preference plus unpaid dividends, except for Series B and Series L which lack early redemption rights. Ownership is generally held via depositary shares representing fractional interests in preferred stock, with dividend payment frequencies and minimum rates varying by series as detailed in the table footnotes.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and BAC disclose general redemption rights for their preferred stock series at the corporation's option. MS states that Series E, F, and I are redeemable on dividend payment dates or following a regulatory capital treatment event. BAC states that it may redeem most preferred stock series at its option at liquidation preference plus declared and unpaid dividends, but explicitly notes exceptions where Series B and L lack early redemption rights. Both filings use similar language for the general 'option' to redeem, but BAC provides a broader summary of rights across most series including specific exclusion of certain series, while MS focuses on the specific triggers for Series E, F, and I.

sentences.text: Series E, F and I are currently redeemable, and all other Series are redeemable, at the Firm's option (i) in whole or in part, from time to time, on any dividend payment date on or after the redemption date or (ii) in whole but not in part at any time within 90 days following a regulatory capital treatment event (as described in the terms of that series).
(2)The Corporation may redeem series of preferred stock on or after the redemption date, in whole or in part, at its option, at the liquidation preference plus declared and unpaid dividends.
Series B and Series L Preferred Stock do not have early redemption/call rights.

peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidates for C (c_2024_8_D442 and c_2024_8_D427) discuss the redemption of specific series (Series U and Series D) that have already been redeemed or are marked as not applicable. The C disclosures are retrospective records of completed redemptions rather than prospective rights descriptions.

comparisons.peer_topic: 2025 Issuance of Series Z Preferred Stock
comparisons.peer_summary: In January 2025, the firm issued 76,000 shares of Series Z 6.85% Fixed-Rate Reset Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock, which has a $25,000 liquidation preference, is redeemable at the firm's option starting February 10, 2030, and pays semi-annual dividends at 6.85% per annum until that date, thereafter resetting to 2.461% plus the five-year treasury rate.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and GS describe specific preferred stock series that are redeemable at the firm's option. MS notes Series E, F, and I are redeemable on dividend payment dates or after a regulatory capital treatment event. GS describes Series Z as redeemable at the firm's option beginning on a specific future date (February 10, 2030). Both disclosures indicate the redemption is at the firm's option, but MS highlights the 'regulatory capital treatment event' trigger common to many series, while GS highlights a fixed future date for the newly issued Series Z.

sentences.text: Series E, F and I are currently redeemable, and all other Series are redeemable, at the Firm's option (i) in whole or in part, from time to time, on any dividend payment date on or after the redemption date or (ii) in whole but not in part at any time within 90 days following a regulatory capital treatment event (as described in the terms of that series).

Each share of Series Z Preferred Stock issued and outstanding has a liquidation preference of $25,000 per share, is represented by 25 depositary shares and is redeemable at the firm's option beginning February 10, 2030 at a redemption price equal to $25,000 per share plus declared and unpaid dividends.

comparisons.peer_summary: JPMorgan's preferred stock series may be redeemed on dividend payment dates on or after their earliest redemption date, or following a capital treatment event. All redemptions are subject to non-objection from the Federal Reserve.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and JPM disclose that their preferred stock series are redeemable at the firm's option on dividend payment dates or following a regulatory/capital treatment event. A key difference is that JPM explicitly states that all redemptions are subject to non-objection from the Federal Reserve, whereas MS's selected text for this specific series description does not mention the Federal Reserve approval requirement in that sentence, though it does mention regulatory capital treatment events.

sentences.text: Series E, F and I are currently redeemable, and all other Series are redeemable, at the Firm's option (i) in whole or in part, from time to time, on any dividend payment date on or after the redemption date or (ii) in whole but not in part at any time within 90 days following a regulatory capital treatment event (as described in the terms of that series).
Each series of the Firm's preferred stock may be redeemed on any dividend payment date on or after the earliest redemption date for that series.
All outstanding preferred stock series may also be redeemed following a "capital treatment event," as described in the terms of each series.
Any redemption of the Firm's preferred stock is subject to non-objection from the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (the "Federal Reserve").
